You have two rooks that can coordinate. After White moved the knight to f4, it blocked escape squares. Your check on h4 forces the king to g1, and then Rg8+ drives the knight to g6 to block. This knight placement allows you to win the h5 pawn cleanly. The lesson: when your opponent's pieces are tightly packed, forcing checks often reveal tactical weaknesses and allow your pieces to harvest material.
